calls.head: Forecheck vs. Patience
calls.body: The Hurricanes hound the puck, but the Bruins sit back. Carolina is one of the league’s best for forecheck pressure, and Boston is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect the Hurricanes to win more pucks back deep in the Bruins’ end.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Kochetkov wins his first eight, tying a Hurricanes record
paras: Pavel Zacha got the scoring started for the Bruins on the power play a minute and a half in, and that was all they would get. Nicolas Deslauriers and Tanner Jeannot squared off midway through the first, and Jackson Blake tied it up for Carolina late in the period. The Bruins went more than 20 minutes without a shot on goal, from early in the second to midway through the third, while the Hurricanes put twelve on net. Most teams don’t go that long without a shot even once a season. Sebastian Aho put the Hurricanes ahead for good midway through the third.

The Hurricanes carried the play, outshooting the Bruins 30-15 (25-9 at 5-on-5), and got the result to match. Pyotr Kochetkov needed only 14 saves for the Canes, and Jeremy Swayman kept the Bruins in it, stopping 28 of 30. Kochetkov has won all eight of his starts this season, matching Frederik Andersen (2021-22) for the longest winning run to open a season by any goalie in franchise history.

The Bruins killed off a two-man advantage that lasted less than two minutes late in the second. The Hurricanes improved to 10-2-2 and took the best points percentage in the NHL from the Bruins, who dropped to 9-3-1. That leaves the Hurricanes first in the NHL in both points and points percentage.

items.text: The Bruins’ eight-game point streak is over.
The chances caught up with the Bruins this time. Their record (.792) had been well ahead of what their chances were worth (.588).
The Hurricanes have won eight of their last ten.
Mark Jankowski’s six-game point streak ended.
